anf_compare.notes: No ANF or other public-domain English of this homily; translated from the Greek.

bible_refs.note: τὸ σκάνδαλον τῶν Ἰουδαίων … τὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν μωρίαν echoes 1 Corinthians 1:23, Ἰουδαίοις μὲν σκάνδαλον, ἔθνεσιν δὲ μωρίαν; Paul's own words are applied to Paul, so the citation stands at the close of the clause.

Pharaoh drowned while pursuing Israel: the Egyptians pursue (κατεδίωξαν, Exodus 14:23) and are covered by the sea (14:28). καταποντόω is also the verb of the Song in Exodus 15:4 LXX (κατεπόντισεν ἐν ἐρυθρᾷ θαλάσσῃ); the narrative range is cited.

Adam stretching out his hands to the tree and drawing death on us is the Fall (Genesis 3:6). The wording of 'stretching out the hand' to the tree echoes Genesis 3:22 LXX (μήποτε ἐκτείνῃ τὴν χεῖρα), which is noted but not cited inline.

Ἀμήν, ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω σοι ὅτι σήμερον μετ' ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ: Luke 23:43 has a single Ἀμήν and no γάρ/ὅτι (Ἀμήν σοι λέγω, σήμερον μετ' ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ). Hesychius doubles the Amen in the Johannine manner; the English keeps 'truly, truly' as he has it.

choices.why: βασιλεύουσα ('the reigning city') is the standard title of the imperial capital.

choices.english: he took up as a safeguard of wisdom
choices.why: φυλακτήριον is a protective charm; 'safeguard' keeps the sense without an occult tone, and 'took up' renders the middle of ἐπισπάω.
rejected: drew to himself an amulet of wisdom

choices.why: The copy-text has ἀπελαύνω ('drive away'); the easy correction ἐπήλασεν ('brought on') is noted but not adopted.

choices.english: hurled the thief into paradise like a javelin
choices.why: ἀκοντίζω is 'throw a javelin'; the image of speed is kept.
rejected: sent the thief swiftly into paradise

pass_a_gloss: [continuing from u01-open, whose 'then across the world's…' runs on here] circle he shone upon. See for me, beloved, the reigning Rome with symbols of the cross in the middle of the marketplace being made stately / taking pride. See for me Paul composing immortal letters and having written down himself slave of the cross; he was not ashamed of the cross, the stumbling block of the Jews; the foolishness of the nations he drew to himself as safeguard / amulet of wisdom; in wood of cross he roused up the churches of the inhabited world. One rod Mosaic drove away the scourges / plagues of the Egyptians, but a rod by kinship toward the wood of the cross stops the sins of humans. There Pharaoh is sunk in the sea pursuing Israel; here the devil is undone, and the worshippers of the Savior are saved. There, stretching out the hands, Adam drew upon us death, but our Master by the stretching out of the hands saved through all things. But O wood more magnificent than heaven and surpassing the heavenly vaults; O wood thrice-blessed ferrying across our souls into heaven; O wood having provided for the world salvation and having driven out a devilish army; O wood having hurled like a javelin a robber into paradise and having made him dance with Christ: 'Amen, amen for I say to you that today with me you will be in the paradise.' Let us imitate of the man-slayer the good mind / resolve, or rather of the Spirit-bearer [continues in u01-rem-mid].
pass_b_english: Look, beloved, at Rome, the imperial city, glorying in the emblems of the cross in the middle of her marketplace. Look at Paul, writing his undying letters and recording himself as a servant of the cross. He was not ashamed of the cross, the stumbling block of the Jews; what the Gentiles call foolishness he took up as a safeguard of wisdom (1 Corinthians 1:23). By the wood of the cross he roused the churches throughout the world.

A single rod of Moses drove off the plagues of the Egyptians, but a rod akin to the wood of the cross puts an end to the sins of humankind. There Pharaoh is drowned in the sea while pursuing Israel (Exodus 14:23–28); here the devil is overthrown, and those who worship the Savior are saved. There Adam stretched out his hands and drew death upon us (Genesis 3:6); but our Master, by stretching out his hands, saved all things.

But O wood, more magnificent than heaven and higher than the vaults of the sky! O thrice-blessed wood, ferrying our souls across to heaven! O wood that won salvation for the world and drove out the devil's army! O wood that hurled the thief into paradise like a javelin and set him dancing with Christ: 'For truly, truly I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise' (Luke 23:43).
Let us imitate the good resolve of the murderer, or rather of the bearer of the Spirit…
source_text:
κύκλῳ κατέ λαμψεν.
3 Ἰδέ μοι, ἀγαπητέ, τὴν βασιλεύουσαν Ῥώμην σταυροῦ συμ-βόλοις ἐν μέσῳ
τῆς ἀγορᾶς σεμνυνομένην. Ἰδέ μοι Παῦλον ἀθα νάτους ἐπιστολὰς συγγραφόμενον
καὶ δοῦλον τοῦ σταυροῦ ἑαυ τὸν καταγράψαντα· οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη τὸν σταυρόν, τὸ
σκάν δαλον τῶν Ἰουδαίων· τὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν μω ρίαν σοφίας ἐπεσπάσατο
φυλακτήριον· ἐν σταυροῦ ξύλῳ τὰς τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐκκλησίας διήγειρεν. Μία
ῥάβδος μωσαϊκὴ τὰς τῶν Αἰγυπτίων μάστιγας ἀπήλασεν, ῥάβδος δὲ συγ γενείᾳ πρὸς
τὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ ξύλον παύει τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἁ μαρτήματα. Ἐκεῖ Φαραὼ
καταποντοῦται τὸν Ἰσραὴλ καταδιώκων, ἐνταῦθα δὲ διάβολος καταλύεται, οἱ δὲ τοῦ
σωτῆρος προσκυνηταὶ σῴζονται. Ἐκεῖ τὰς χεῖρας ἐκτεί νας ὁ Ἀδὰμ θάνατον ἡμῖν
ἐπεσπάσατο, ὁ δὲ ἡμέτερος δεσπότης τῇ τῶν χειρῶν ἐκτάσει τὰ πάντα διέσωσεν.
4 Ἀλλ' ὦ ξύλον μεγαλοπρεπέστερον οὐρανοῦ καὶ τὰς οὐρα νίους ἁψῖδας
ὑπερβάλλον, ὦ ξύλον τρισμακάριστον τὰς ἡμετέρας ψυχὰς διαπορθμεῦον εἰς
οὐρανόν, ὦ ξύλον τῷ κόσμῳ τὴν σωτηρίαν πορισάμενον καὶ στρατὸν διαβολικὸν
ἐκδιῶξαν, ὦ ξύλον λῃστὴν εἰς παράδεισον ἀκοντίσαν καὶ μετὰ Χριστοῦ χορεύειν
πεποιηκός· «Ἀμήν, ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω σοι ὅτι σήμερον μετ' ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ.»
Μιμησώμεθα τοῦ ἀνδροφόνου τὴν ἀγαθὴν γνώμην, μᾶλλον δὲ τοῦ πνευματοφόρου
source_normalizations: Soft and line-break splits joined (κατέ λαμψεν, συμ-βόλοις, ἀθα νάτους, ἑαυ τὸν, σκάν δαλον, μω ρίαν, συγ γενείᾳ, ἁ μαρτήματα, ἐκτεί νας, οὐρα νίους); no letters added.
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Row opens mid-sentence ('…whole circle he shone out.'), completing 'then across the world's…' at the end of u01-open, and closes mid-sentence before διὰ τὴν μετὰ ταῦτα πίστιν in u01-rem-mid.

Every clause checked against the Greek: Rome and its crosses, Paul the servant of the cross, the rod of Moses and the rod of the cross, Pharaoh and the devil, Adam's hands and the Master's hands, the four 'O wood' acclamations, and the call to imitate the thief.
Reviewer fixes applied in tr0: 'whole circle' at the join, 'throughout the world' (no 'whole' in τῆς οἰκουμένης), and 'but' for δέ against Moses' rod.
Scripture checked: 1 Corinthians 1:23, Exodus 14:23–28, Genesis 3:6, Luke 23:43. Romans 1:16, Galatians 6:14 and Genesis 3:22 LXX are possible echoes only and are not cited inline.
